To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the C4 gene, which encodes the pathogenicity determinant of begomovirusses, has been shown to evolve rapidly, and that the C4 of a new begovirus species was acquired by recombination, allowing the virus to dispense with its requirement for a betatellite.
a new begomvirus species, TLCYn V, has evolved from TYLCCCNV by recombination and that it is more virulent than TYLCCCNV because it encodes a more virulent version of the C4 protein.

a recombinant begovirus resulting from the exchange of the C3 gene has a more effective suppressor of silencing protein, allowing the begovirus to infect a range of plant hosts without the aid of a betasattelite.

the identification of a recombinant begomoovirus that is representative of a new species, and the characterisation of its genome and the C4 gene, which is involved in symptom induction and suppression of host defence responses.
the molecular biology of plant viruses and the development of novel strategies for the control of plant viral diseases.
